name: 4-coil Shakti: amygdala left + hippocampus right, synchronized (30 min)
summary: Murphy's stereo Shakti session in its 'synchronized' form: the amygdala signal on the left temporal lobe and the hippocampal signal on the right play at the same time. Murphy presents it as positive emotion (left amygdala) plus positive cognition (right hippocampus).
setting: Evenings: the vendor says sessions are 'usually better after the sun goes down'. Darkness and quiet (the vendor says effects during a session need darkness and silence); eyes closed, relaxed, without meditating or falling asleep; no meditation, mind machines or drugs at the same time.
schedule: Vendor's Shakti rules: at most every 72 h or once a week, never on consecutive days; a series of 3 or 6 sessions, then a 21-day break; try a session 2-3 times before changing it.
notes: 4-coil Shakti layout: the left stereo channel's two coils on the left temporal lobe (FT7, TP7) and the right channel's two on the right (FT8, TP8), static, with no rotation or alternation; the vendor says only 'left channel coils on the left side, right channel on the right' (temporal or temporo-frontal), so the sites are an inference. The vendor gives no coil polarity for this 4-coil layout (the one + and one − coil per pair is documented only for the 8 Coil Shakti), so both coils of a side are driven with the same polarity here. Synchronized: both signals start together every 4.69 s, each followed by about 4 s of silence (Shakti's standard latency). Both signal files are proprietary: the amygdala 'burstx' file is approximated by the built-in accelerating burst (6 to 30 Hz), 230 points of 3 ms (0.69 s, the published 230-point burst-firing length at Shakti's standard 3-ms points); the hippocampal 'LTP' file by 4 theta bursts, each of 4 biphasic pulses 9 ms apart (after the 4-pulse 100 Hz bursts of Larson & Lynch), repeated every 186 ms (5.4 Hz, the spectral peak the vendor reports for its LTP signal), on 3-ms points (0.74 s). Other forms of this session: murphy-shakti-amyl-hippr-variants-sequence (taking turns) and murphy-shakti-amyl-hippr-variants-slow (alternative slow hippocampal signal). Murphy aims the left amygdala signal at positive emotion and the right hippocampal signal at positive cognition, a vendor reading extended from small Persinger-lab studies (Persinger, Richards & Koren 1994: LTP-pattern fields over the right hemisphere were rated more pleasant than over the left). Murphy reports male users feeling 'energized' and describing better 'verbal/mathematical/logical skills'; these are testimonials. One negative report followed sessions longer than suggested, so keep to 30 min and the schedule. Murphy reports headache or pressure in about 2% of users of an earlier version of the technology, mostly with hippocampal signals; if so, lower the intensity by one third. Independent double-blind tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012, the latter with the 8 Coil Shakti amygdala signal). Not for people with epilepsy; stop at once if distressed.
